text: You have a sorted list of a million names. How many looks does it take to find one?
Here are sixteen numbers in order, and we are looking for forty-two.
Look at the middle one first. It says thirty, so forty-two must be to the right.
In one look, half the list is gone. These eight numbers can't hold it.
Do it again on what is left. The middle says fifty, so now go left.
Four numbers, then two, then one. Forty-two, found in four looks.
Every look cuts the list in half, so doubling the list adds just one more look.
A million names? Twenty looks is enough.
